findings.what: Ledger trap for the next CI stack name, plus a new fact on CI queueing. EXP_RULES maps exp8\d[a-z]* to safetail (9.5 h). A stack such as exp78b + CI will naturally be named exp82*, so it would get the wrong family: 'UNPROVEN/REJECT' at L 9.6-10.5 h and a spurious 'v', where safetail_ci admits up to 10.75 h. New fact: the exp79a dummy did NOT wait 2-3.3 h in the queue. It was 404 at 20:33Z (round-20 judge) and PASS was logged at 21:26Z with kernel ~1,712 s. So a CI-stack dummy pushed after the exp78b read (~07:40Z) can plausibly pass before 12:00Z, but not reliably. The metadata equals exp70g's except for the dataset, with the same NvidiaTeslaT4 shape and docker 37c64f7d.

findings.what: 29 Sep window problem: E10 has no slot, and W4 cannot fit 5 spaced files. (a) The E10 v3 watch loop runs until 29 Sep 12:00Z, but the last submit is 01:45Z 29 Sep (v2 (7)) and W4 may use all 5 slots. A trigger between 02:00 and 12:00Z 29 Sep, the period when late public notebooks tend to appear, therefore has neither a slot nor a rule, even though the user's E10 v3 says 'as fast as possible'. (b) W4 allows <= 5 files in 00:05-01:45Z, but v2 (4) keeps K2-like files >= 40 min apart so the count-rule UP test stays separable. That leaves room for at most 3 K2-like files (00:05/00:45/01:25), plus CI files, which complete ~2 h later.
